correctness.rationale: The number K=floor(L/2) of extra starting-vertex visits has tails P(K≥j)=t^j with t=(1−p)². For any two-walk coupling, Var((K1+K2)/2)=(μ+E K1K2)/2, μ=t/(1−t). Layer-cake and Fréchet give E K1K2 ≥ J(t)=Σ_{j,k≥1}(t^j+t^k−1)_+, and the inverse-CDF antitone coupling attains each event intersection bound simultaneously. Stagewise survival has P(L1≥u,L2≥v)=r^{min(u,v)}q^{|u−v|}, r=(1−2p)_+; summing even tails yields M_stage=r²(1+t)/((1−r²)(1−t)). The strict p<1/2 loss follows already from j=k=1 excess (with no negative excess elsewhere). The p=1/3 triple (2/5,9/16,18/25) and 5 rational cases were independently checked. With ε=1−t, εK(U)→−log(1−U), εK(1−U)→−log U and dominated convergence gives ∫log u log(1−u)du=2−π²/6. Universal optimality rests on the full Fréchet proof, not finite tests.

evidence: General OT permits coupling of geometric lengths on any graph; Fréchet–Hoeffding provides classical countermonotone monotone-cost optimum.
Reid et al. use quantile permutations and approximations and do not supply the all-p exact stepwise comparison on the two-state linear Green objective.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general technique is broader than the model class, but does not give the bespoke exact stepwise collision term, two thresholds or 2−π²/6 ratio without further calculation.

evidence: Global quantile coupling is prior known; direct theorem reduces K=floor(L/2) to monotone geometric tails.
Stepwise overlap M_stage and the rare-stopping limit require independent moment summation/integral.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Existing general coupling results imply possibility of improvement but do not, as stated, dominate this all-p exact numerical benchmark. Retain precedence uncertainty for uninspected specialized appendices.

evidence: Reid et al. section 4 approximates optimal transport for graph random features and feature-pair bilinear kernel estimates.
Current objective is (Z1+Z2)/2 of one Green-resolvent diagonal, not a graph-kernel bilinear form.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The same random-walk length marginal and antithetic terminology do not identify different cost functionals; no equivalence between the claimed exact M=E K1K2 and their nonlinear objective was shown.

Earlier graph-feature papers optimize a bilinear kernel/feature cost, not this single-walk linear Green diagonal with exact unrestricted p thresholds and rare-stopping ratio. A hidden specialized marginal coupling example remains possible.

value.rationale: An exact optimization over ALL legal joint length laws on the simplest nontrivial walk gives a reference benchmark for stagewise antithetic algorithms, identifies two distinct parameter thresholds and quantifies the asymptotic efficiency gap. The two-state graph is motivated as the minimal nontrivial resolvent test, and explicit sharp all-p comparisons are not merely a renamed textbook formula.

final_claim: For a two-walker unbiased diagonal Green entry estimator on one edge with geometric walk lengths, inverse-CDF countermonotonicity gives the unrestricted minimal variance V*=(μ+J(q²))/2; stagewise half-cycle antithetic stopping is strictly worse exactly for p<1/2, with a separate p=1−1/√2 no-joint-revisit boundary.
